1. **`src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.CSharp.targets` (new `PropertyGroup`)** — The condition `'$(_IsNETCoreOrNETStandard)' == 'true'` suppresses CS8002 for .NET Standard targets too, but the PR title/description explicitly say the fix is for "modern .NET TFMs" and that ".NET Standard … will continue to receive CS8002." .NET Standard assemblies are routinely consumed by .NET Framework apps, where strong-name validation is still enforced, so blanket-suppressing there can hide a legitimate warning. Restrict the condition to `.NETCoreApp` only (e.g. `'$(TargetFrameworkIdentifier)' == '.NETCoreApp'`), matching what the description claims was implemented, and update the test file's netstandard2.0/2.1 cases to assert CS8002 is **not** suppressed (move them into the "not suppressed" theory alongside net472/net48).

2. **Same `PropertyGroup`** — The PR description says detection uses a `TargetFrameworkIdentifier` check, but the diff instead references `_IsNETCoreOrNETStandard`, a property that is never defined anywhere in this diff. If that property isn't already defined elsewhere in the SDK, it evaluates to empty/false and the whole suppression — and the "all tests pass" claim — would be false. Replace it with an explicit, visible condition in this file (e.g. `'$(TargetFrameworkIdentifier)' == '.NETCoreApp'`) so the logic is self-contained and verifiable, rather than depending on an opaque pre-existing property.

3. **Same `PropertyGroup`, XML comment** — The comment says suppression applies "for .NET Core and .NET Standard TFMs," which contradicts the PR's stated scope and compounds the confusion from #1/#2. Fix the comment once the condition is corrected so it accurately describes only .NETCoreApp targets.

4. **No opt-out / no breaking-change note** — This silently changes build warning output for every net6.0+ project SDK-wide, which can affect consumers who assert on warning counts/logs or use `/warnaserror` patterns relying on CS8002. Add a breaking-change/release-note entry for this behavior change, consistent with SDK convention for changes that alter default build output, even though the behavior itself was requested by the linked issue.

5. **`test/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tests/GivenThatWeWantToSuppressCS8002Warning.cs`** — No test verifies the suppression is scoped to C# only (the issue explicitly calls out "C# is the project language" as a condition, which is why this lives in `CSharp.targets` rather than a shared targets file). Add a regression test with an F# or VB project confirming CS8002 is unaffected there, so a future refactor that moves this logic to a shared targets file is caught.
